summary: Esho Yamaguchi studied at Kyoto University and worked in the fields of Indology and philosophy. He held posts at Ritsumeikan University and Osaka University, where he served as professor (attested 1980–1984).
A scholar in Buddhist studies, Eshun Otsuka studied at Taisho University as a research student and held a research student post there, attested in 2013.

Estela Piccin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She completed degrees at the State University of Campinas, Associação Buddha-Dharma, Methodist University of São Paulo, and Buddha-Dharma Centre of Hong Kong, later teaching art in Campinas.

Ester Bianchi is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied under Alfredo Cadonna and Jean-Noël Robert at Ca' Foscari University and EPHE, later holding faculty positions at Florence and Perugia, with visiting appointments at Berkeley.
Ethan Kroll is an Indologist who served on the editorial board of Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies and held a position at Baker McKenzie, both attested in 2012.
Etienne Vermeersch was a philosopher who studied at Ghent University between circa 1953 and 1958. He subsequently held a faculty post at Ghent University from 1967 to 1997.
Working in Indology and philosophy, Etsuaki Teraishi held posts as an associate professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and as a JSPS special research fellow (attested 2001).

Indologist Eugen Hultzsch studied at Leipzig and Bonn under scholars including Ernst Windisch and Georg Bühler. He served as Government Epigraphist in India (1886–1903) and later held the chair of Sanskrit at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1903–1925).

Eugen Pander was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who studied at Polytechnikum Riga. From 1881 to 1889, he served as Professor of National Economy and Lecturer of Russian and German at Tongwen Guan.

Eugen Prym worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin, Leipzig under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer, and Bonn under Johann Gildemeister, where he became Privatdozent of Oriental Languages in 1870.

Eugen Rose was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. He studied at the University of Königsberg in 1929, the University of Bonn (Ph.D., 1929–1933), and the University of Marburg (dr.theol., 1929–1941).

Eugen Wilhelm was an Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological linguist. He studied at Halle and Jena under August Schleicher, later teaching at schools in Eisenach and Jena before becoming an honorary professor at the University of Jena in 1897.

Eugene N. Lane worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Princeton University and Harvard University, later holding academic posts at the University of Virginia (circa 1961–1966) and the University of Missouri (circa 1966–2000).

Eugene Watson Burlingame specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Yale and Pennsylvania, he also studied under Charles Rockwell Lanman at Harvard and Maurice Bloomfield at Johns Hopkins, later lecturing in Pāli at Yale (1917–1932).

Eugene Y. Wang is a scholar of art history, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. After studying under Hung Wu and John M. Rosenfield, he taught at the University of Chicago before becoming the Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Professor at Harvard University.
Eugeni d'Ors was a philosopher who studied at the University of Barcelona (circa 1897–1903) and Universidad Central (circa 1903–1905). He held a post at Universidad Central from circa 1944 to 1954.

Eugenia Vanina is an Indologist and historian. She earned her Ph.D. from Moscow State University (1975–1981) and joined the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences as a researcher in 1985.

Eugenio Frola, active in Indology and mathematics, studied engineering and mathematics at the Polytechnic University of Turin and University of Turin. He taught mathematics at the Polytechnic University of Turin from circa 1934 to 1962.
Eugenius Marius Uhlenbeck was a linguist who studied at Leiden University from circa 1932 to 1941. He later served as a professor at Leiden University from 1950 to 1983.

Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Jagiellonian University, Lviv, and in Paris under Meillet and Lévi. He held posts at Lviv, Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń, and as Professor of Indology at Warsaw (1953–1971).
